roots.context: In this unit you tested a model beak and looked for a dinosaur's features on a bird. Here we ask what it means that a kind of animal can change, and still be the same family.

deep_truth.truth: In Find the Dinosaur in a Bird, you saw scaly feet, three front toes and a walk on tiptoe. Fossils show small meat-eating dinosaurs with the same feet, and with feathers and wishbones too. Birds are the one branch of the dinosaur family that lived through the asteroid strike. So dinosaurs are still alive, and one may be sitting on your window grill now.
deep_truth.habit: We say 'the dinosaurs died out' and treat birds as a separate kind of animal. The family tree puts birds inside the dinosaurs. So that sentence is true only of the other dinosaurs.
deep_truth.evidence: In Find the Dinosaur in a Bird, you checked eight features on a bird. All eight are also found in fossils of small theropods. In the game Bird, Old Dinosaur or Both, 11 of the 16 feature cards belong to both.

three.who_am_i: You belong to a very old family of animals. Your backbone, your four limbs and your five fingers come from animals who lived before the first dinosaur.
three.what_is_life: Life does not start from nothing with each new kind of animal. A hen still has scaly feet, feathers and a nest, which came from her dinosaur ancestors and changed a little.
three.what_is_this_world: The animals you see are not a finished set. Each kind is one stage in a change that is still going on, as the finches showed after one drought.

roots.thread: Every bird hatched from an egg laid by a mother who hatched from an egg. Follow that line of mothers back for 150 million years, and they are feathered dinosaurs. Follow the line further, and it reaches the first animals and then the first cells. Many wise teachers taught that all living beings share one life. The fossils tell a similar story in their own way. Every kind of living being belongs to one family, and that family has been changing slowly for a very long time.

teachings.teaching: Some blind men each touch one part of an elephant. One says an elephant is like a pot, another like a pillar, another like a broom. Each is sure, and they quarrel.
teachings.link: In 1836 Edward Hitchcock studied three-toed footprints in rock and said giant birds made them. Later scientists said dinosaurs made them. Each side held part of the truth, like the men with the elephant. The three-toed feet belong to dinosaurs, and birds are a kind of dinosaur.

teachings.source: Heraclitus, as quoted by Plato in Cratylus 402a
teachings.teaching: Everything moves and nothing stays still. You cannot step twice into the same river.
teachings.link: A kind of animal is like a river, which never stands still. The finches of Daphne Major had deeper beaks after one drought. The name 'finch' stayed the same, but the birds had changed.

teachings.source: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1859), the last sentence
teachings.teaching: From a simple beginning, endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
teachings.link: Darwin wrote 'are being'. The change from a small feathered dinosaur to a sparrow has not stopped. Beaks are still being fitted to foods today.

science.text: All living things share one ancestor. The same chemical code is used in the cells of a sparrow, a neem tree and you.
Scientists do not agree on what a 'kind' or species really is. Some say kinds are real units in nature. Others say they are lines that people draw across slow change.

other_view.who: Many people of faith, in several religions
other_view.view: Every kind of creature was made in the form they have now, and a bird has always been a bird. On this view, the likeness between a hen and a small dinosaur shows one maker's plan, and not one family.

practice.title: One minute with a living dinosaur
practice.say: Find a bird you can see well. Watch her for one minute without speaking. Look at the scaly feet, the quick turns of the head and the eye. Now stand on your toes and fold your arms like wings. Feel your backbone, your ankles and your fingers. She has the same bones as you, in different lengths. How does it feel to share a skeleton with her?
practice.kid: Watch one bird for a minute. Look at her feet and her eye. Stand on your toes. Fold your arms like wings. You and she share the same bones.

ask: In Find the Dinosaur in a Bird, you ticked the same features for a hen and for Velociraptor. Where does 'dinosaur' stop and 'bird' begin?
The finches' beaks changed after one drought. Is a kind of animal a fixed thing, or something that is happening?
A godwit, a sparrow and you share a backbone from one ancestor. What does 'family' mean to you now?

playtest: Read through as a parent and child in a city flat would use it, step by step, but not yet done at home. The Beak Lever Test (core) needs ordinary paper scissors, two sheets of newspaper and a ruler. With most scissors the tips cut 4 to 8 layers of newspaper and the part near the hinge cuts 16 or more. Blunt or very small scissors give lower numbers, but the order stays the same, so the steps say to record what really happens. A grown-up should stay beside the child for the cuts. Beak and Feet Watch and Find the Dinosaur in a Bird (both core) work at any window where a crow or a pigeon comes. If no bird comes, a phone video of a hen or a pigeon walking does the same job. The wishbone is optional, for families who cook chicken. The Frozen Mud Test needs a freezer and about two cups of wet soil from a plant pot. Wet sand or used tea leaves work if there is no soil. The mud must be wet enough to shine, or it will not freeze hard. Freeze it overnight. On a hot day the top thaws in less than 20 minutes, so the counts after thawing will be higher than in the example. The Sleeping Grip uses only the child's own hand, and works for nearly everyone if the hand is kept loose. Stick a Nest to a Wall works with sticky soil. Soil that crumbles will not hold, and then stiff dough made from old atta is the alternative. The nest needs a full day to dry. The two card games need only the printed cards and some dried beans. No part needs a garden, a park or a pet. Facts to treat with care: the finch numbers (about 1,200 before the 1977 drought, about 180 after, and beaks about half a millimetre deeper) are the usual rounded figures. The ages of the fossils are rounded. Several points are marked as debated or as ideas. These are whether Archaeopteryx was a bird, whether Tyrannosaurus had feathers and how flight began. The reasons some birds lived through the asteroid strike are marked in the same way. So is the use of the toe lock in sleep. In the game Bird, Old Dinosaur or Both, the card about swallowed stones rests on a few fossils. The Heraclitus line is a paraphrase of Plato's report. The story's godwit is a real kind of bird and a real winter visitor to Indian wetlands, but her landing on a terrace is made up. The three videos have no address yet.
